# HRD-I-0001

<!-- Generated by `mustur export`. Do not hand-edit: `mustur verify` fails on drift, and the store is the record. -->

**Group save sharing is worth building, and worth building inside Hoard rather than alone**

investigation · 2026-09-13

work: [HRD-W-0001](../work-units/HRD-W-0001.md#hrd-w-0001)

## Context

Asked 2026-09-13: Pie's idea was a Steam feature, cloud saves shareable with friends so a co-op group can rotate who hosts a world (Valheim) without paying for a server. Steam has no such feature: Steam Cloud is per user per game (partner.steamgames.com/doc/features/cloud), the request has sat on Steam's forums since at least 2020 with no Valve reply, and Grounded 1 and 2 ship exactly this on Xbox cloud, which shows people want it. The hard parts are not storage: two hosts at once forking the save, saves bound to the host's identity (Palworld rebinds player GUIDs on a host change), quota ownership, trusting a file a friend controls, and mods. Existing tools: SaveSync (paid, Windows with a Linux beta, 54 games, Steam Workshop storage), Hearth (free, MIT, Windows-only, Google Drive, locks every shared world on launch), CoopSync (free, Windows, 2 games), palrelay and valleysave (one game each). Hoard (rleeon/hoard, AGPL-3.0, 103 stars, one maintainer answering issues within two days) already runs on Windows, Linux, macOS and SteamOS, versions every save, self-hosts, and detects 20,000+ games from the Ludusavi manifest, but syncs one person's own devices only. Verdict: a standalone tool is not distinct enough; group sharing added to Hoard is. Pie then asked for launch-time locking to be replaced, because a launch lock would lock every shared world a player has across groups (Hearth's flaw); the resulting design is in HRD-W-0001.

## Verdict

build it into a DevOfPie fork of Hoard, self-hosted first
